subject.title: [Bug]:  Isolated cron session agent loop continues consuming tokens after run marked "ok"

question: Should recurring isolated cron jobs clean up their per-run sessions by default, or should `deleteAfterRun` remain a one-shot-only contract?
rationale: Current main supports recurring isolated jobs but does not default cleanup for them; the open linked PR fixes that direction while another open PR rejects the recurring cleanup contract, and automation cannot choose the intended product/API behavior.

options.title: Support recurring isolated cleanup
options.body: Land a reconciled fix that defaults or migrates omitted isolated recurring cleanup safely while preserving explicit opt-out or clear operator recovery.

options.title: Choose one-shot-only cleanup
options.body: Reject recurring `deleteAfterRun` as an API contract and close or redirect the recurring-cleanup PR after Gateway, UI, docs, and recovery paths are aligned.

options.title: Accept fresh-create-only mitigation
options.body: Land the linked PR as only a new-job default and explicitly document that existing omitted jobs require operator action or a separate migration.

recommendation.title: Support recurring isolated cleanup
recommendation.body: Land a reconciled fix that defaults or migrates omitted isolated recurring cleanup safely while preserving explicit opt-out or clear operator recovery.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision crosses cron normalization, persisted store behavior, and user-facing compatibility, and this owner has the strongest recent history across those cron contract surfaces.
